sentences.text: Naim Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 1 November, 2019

Author: Yashwant Varma
Bench: Yashwant Varma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 6
Case :- Writ - C No. - 1910 of 2019
Petitioner :- Naim Ahmad
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Satyendra Narayan Singh,Chandra Nath Bhatt,Kundan Rai
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Yashwant Varma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Court notes that by the order of 20 February 2019 the State respondents were granted three weeks and no more further time for filing a counter affidavit.
Despite that peremptory direction, no counter affidavit has been filed.
Consequently this matter proceeds ex parte.

The petitioner who runs a retail business of selling fish, meat and poultry assails the orders passed by the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 cancelling his licence and sealing the premises from which the business was being conducted.
The record reflects that the Licensing Authority inspected the premises and called upon the petitioner to explain the source from which poultry and meat was being obtained.
Although he was granted 15 days' time to furnish the requisite explanation, no reply appears to have been submitted.

In light of the failure on the part of the petitioner to explain the source from which the poultry items were being obtained, the Licensing Authority proceeded to Naim Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 1 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57654335/
1 cancel the permission accorded to the petitioner under the provisions of the Food Safety Standards Act 2006 by an order of 04 April 2018.

entities.text: Naim Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by that order the petitioner approached the Additional Commissioner.
That revision which was preferred has come to be dismissed by the order of 19 November 2018.

The Court notes that although the original order passed by the Licensing Authority on 04 April 2018 was based solely on the ground of a failure on the part of the petitioner to explain from where the poultry items had been sourced, the Revisional Authority has gone far beyond and has proceeded to hold that the petitioner had also violated paragraphs 7.04 and 9.04 of the sanitary and hygienic requirements for retail meat shops as prescribed under the Act.
It also records that the petitioner had failed to adhere to the hygienic and sanitary conditions which were mandated under the Act and the regulations framed thereunder.

Viewed in that sense, it is manifest that the Revisional Authority has proceeded to record adverse findings against the petitioner on grounds which did not even form part of the original adjudication.
Regard must also be had that even the original notice did not call upon the petitioner to show cause in respect of an alleged violation of hygiene requirements stipulated under the Regulations.

In view thereof, this Court is of the considered opinion that although the order passed by the Revisional Authority would merit being set aside, the Licensing Authority must be granted liberty to examine the premises of the petitioner from the angle of compliance with the requirements placed by statute and to reconsider and review the order of 04 April 2018 if the petitioner is otherwise found to be in compliance with all statutory provisions.

Accordingly the Court provides as under:-
The petitioner shall submit a certified copy of this order before the third respondent within a period of two weeks from today.

On receipt of the order passed by the Court,
the Licensing Authority, the respondent No.3 herein, shall inspect the premises of the petitioner and assess whether it is in compliance with the provisions made in the Act and the Regulations framed thereunder.
The inspection shall be concluded within a period of 15 days therefrom.

On conclusion of that inspection, the Court leaves it open to the respondent No.3 to take an appropriate decision whether the licence of the petitioner should stand revived and the order dated 04 April 2018 reviewed.
A final decision in this respect shall be communicated to the petitioner within a period of two months from the date of presentation of a certified copy of this order.
The order dated 19 November 2018 shall stand set aside.
The order of 04 April 2018 shall abide by the fresh decision which the Licensing Authority shall now take.
Petition shall consequently stand disposed of.
